corresponding certificate so that the third-party services can use HTTPS.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create stage variables in API Gateway with Name="Endpoint-URL" and Value="Company Domain Name" to overwrite the default URL. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
answers.explanation: Stage variables cannot overwrite the default API Gateway URL; this does not set a custom domain with HTTPS properly.

answers.content: Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point the alias record to the Regional API Gateway stage endpoint. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
answers.explanation: Importing the certificate into ACM in us-east-1 is incorrect for a Regional API Gateway endpoint in ca-central-1; also, alias record direction is incomplete.

answers.content: Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: Creating a Regional API Gateway endpoint and associating it with the company's domain name meets the requirement to use the company's domain name with API Gateway. Importing the public certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region (ca-central-1) ensures regional consistency and proper certificate attachment. Attaching the certificate to the API Gateway endpoint enables HTTPS for the custom domain. Configuring Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint is the correct DNS step for this setup.

answers.content: Create a Regional API Gateway endpoint. Associate the API Gateway endpoint with the company's domain name. Import the public certificate associated with the company's domain name into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region. Attach the certificate to the API Gateway APIs. Create Route 53 DNS records with the company's domain name. Point an A record to the company's domain name.
answers.explanation: Importing the certificate into ACM in us-east-1 is incorrect for a Regional endpoint in ca-central-1; the DNS A record pointing to the domain name itself is incorrect.

questions.content:
A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each
approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3. Company policy
requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted.
Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical
business data that is not easy to reproduce. The files are frequently accessed
in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the
first 30 days.
Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier does not provide immediate access, which is required.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA is less durable and less secure for critical data than S3 Standard-IA.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: The files require immediate and frequent access within the first 30 days, so they should stay in S3 Standard initially. After 30 days, files are rarely accessed but still require immediate accessibility, which matches the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access storage class characteristics. S3 Standard-IA provides lower cost than S3 Standard while maintaining instant access, meeting the requirement for immediate accessibility. S3 Glacier classes are archival and do not support immediate access, so they are unsuitable given the immediate accessibility requirement. S3 One Zone-IA is less durable as it stores data in a single Availability Zone, which is riskier compared to S3 Standard-IA's multi-AZ storage, violating best practices for critical business data.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.
answers.explanation: Moving to S3 Glacier after 4 years risks delayed access, violating immediate accessibility requirement.

questions.content:
A company hosts an application on AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by an
Amazon API Gateway API. The Lambda functions save customer data to an Amazon
Aurora MySQL database. Whenever the company upgrades the database, the Lambda
functions fail to establish database connections until the upgrade is complete.
The result is that customer data is not recorded for some of the event.
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that stores customer data that
is created during database upgrades.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Provision an Amazon RDS proxy to sit between the Lambda functions and the database. Configure the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS proxy.
answers.explanation: Provisioning RDS Proxy does not handle database downtime during upgrades; it mainly improves connection management, so it won't prevent data loss.

answers.content: Increase the run time of the Lambda functions to the maximum. Create a retry mechanism in the code that stores the customer data in the database.
answers.explanation: Increasing Lambda runtime and retrying adds delay but does not guarantee data persistence during database unavailability; data loss can still occur.

answers.content: Persist the customer data to Lambda local storage. Configure new Lambda functions to scan the local storage to save the customer data to the database.
answers.explanation: Persisting data to Lambda local storage is insecure and unreliable as the local storage is ephemeral and not recommended for data durability.

answers.content: Store the customer data in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Create a new Lambda function that polls the queue and stores the customer data in the database.
answers.explanation: Storing customer data in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue decouples data ingestion from database availability, ensuring no data is lost during database upgrades. Using a Lambda function to poll the queue and store data in the database provides a managed, serverless, and reliable way to process data asynchronously. This approach aligns with security best practices by not storing credentials in the Lambda local storage or relying on retry logic within Lambda's limited runtime. Managed services like SQS and Lambda provide scalability and fault tolerance, preferred over custom or manual solutions.

questions.content:
A company is using a SQL database to store movie data that is publicly
accessible. The database runs on an Amazon RDS Single-AZ DB instance. A script
runs queries at random intervals each day to record the number of new movies
that have been added to the database. The script must report a final total
during business hours.
The company's development team notices that the database performance is
inadequate for development tasks when the script is running. A solutions
architect must recommend a solution to resolve this issue.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment.
answers.explanation: Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability and failover but do not improve read query performance or reduce load from read operations.

answers.content: Create a read replica of the database. Configure the script to query only the read replica.
answers.explanation: Creating a read replica offloads read traffic from the primary DB instance, improving database performance for development tasks while the script runs. This approach has minimal operational overhead compared to managing Multi-AZ failover or manual export processes. Using a read replica is a managed AWS service feature designed for this purpose, aligning with best practices to reduce load without complexity.

answers.content: Instruct the development team to manually export the entries in the database at the end of each day.
answers.explanation: Manual exporting adds operational overhead and does not solve the performance issue during script execution.

answers.content: Use Amazon ElastiCache to cache the common queries that the script runs against the database.
answers.explanation: Caching with ElastiCache might help but requires additional configuration and management; also, it may not suit random or infrequent queries well.

questions.content:
A solutions architect must design a highly available infrastructure for a
website. The website is powered by Windows web servers that run on Amazon EC2
instances. The solutions architect must implement a solution that can mitigate a
large-scale DDoS attack that originates from thousands of IP addresses. Downtime
is not acceptable for the website.
Which actions should the solutions architect take to protect the website from
such an attack? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use AWS Shield Advanced to stop the DDoS attack.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield detects, mitigates network volumetric, protocol, application layer DDoS attacks on AWS resources. Shield Standard protects automatically; Advanced provides higher protection.

answers.content: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to automatically block the attackers.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service and does not provide automatic blocking of attackers or DDoS mitigation.

answers.content: Configure the website to use Amazon CloudFront for both static and dynamic content.
answers.explanation: CloudFront delivers static, dynamic web content through edge locations, retrieving content from origin servers like Amazon S3 buckets.

answers.content: Use an AWS Lambda function to automatically add attacker IP addresses to VPC network ACLs.
answers.explanation: Manual blocking using AWS Lambda to update VPC network ACLs is a custom solution that lacks scalability and managed protection compared to Shield Advanced and CloudFront.

answers.content: E. Use EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with a target tracking scaling policy that is set to 80% CPU utilization.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 Spot Instances is related to cost optimization and scaling, not DDoS mitigation or availability during attacks.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application
consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets. The
database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a
private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company.
How should security groups be configured in this situation? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.explanation: Correct and necessary to allow the web tier to accept HTTPS traffic from the internet.

answers.content: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
answers.explanation: Outbound traffic on port 443 from the web tier to anywhere is not needed to be restricted or explicitly set; outbound rules are usually open by default.

answers.content: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: Correct to allow the database tier to accept SQL Server traffic only from web tier instances securely.

answers.content: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: Database tier should not have outbound rules restricting traffic to the web tier; also, outbound traffic on port 443 from database to web tier is unnecessary.

answers.content: E. Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
answers.explanation: Allowing inbound traffic on port 443 to the database tier is not required and violates security best practices.

questions.content:
A hospital recently deployed a RESTful API with Amazon API Gateway and AWS
Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports that are in
PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital needs to modify the Lambda code to
identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
answers.explanation: Using existing Python libraries requires custom development and ongoing maintenance, increasing operational overhead and potential security risks.

answers.content: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
answers.explanation: Using SageMaker for PHI detection requires building and maintaining custom machine learning models, which adds significant operational overhead compared to using managed Comprehend Medical.

answers.content: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
answers.explanation: Amazon Textract is the managed AWS service designed to extract text from documents such as PDFs and images, which fits the use case of processing reports in PDF and JPEG formats. Amazon Comprehend Medical is a specialized managed service that identifies protected health information (PHI) from extracted text, aligning with the need to detect PHI with minimal operational overhead. Using both Textract and Comprehend Medical leverages managed services, reducing the need for maintenance and operational complexity. Options that rely on custom code or other services either increase operational overhead or do not specialize in PHI detection.

answers.content: Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
answers.explanation: Amazon Rekognition is not designed for text extraction from documents; Textract is the appropriate managed service for text extraction.

questions.content:
A company wants to run applications in containers in the AWS Cloud. These
applications are stateless and can tolerate disruptions within the underlying
infrastructure. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and operational
overhead.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
answers.explanation: Running EC2 Auto Scaling groups manually increases operational overhead compared to managed services like EKS.

answers.content: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.
answers.explanation: Using Spot Instances in an Amazon EKS managed node group aligns with minimizing cost by leveraging cheaper Spot Instances. Amazon EKS provides a fully managed Kubernetes control plane, reducing operational overhead compared to managing EC2 Auto Scaling groups directly. The stateless and disruption-tolerant nature of the application makes Spot Instances suitable as interruptions can be tolerated. Managed services like EKS are preferred over manually managing EC2 Auto Scaling groups according to AWS best practices.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Instances do not minimize cost as effectively as Spot Instances for stateless, disruption-tolerant apps.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Instances increase cost compared to Spot Instances and thus do not minimize cost.

questions.content:
A company has a data ingestion workflow that consists of the following:
• An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications
about new data deliveries
• An AWS Lambda function to process the data and record metadata
The company observes that the ingestion workflow fails occasionally because of
network connectivity issues. When such a failure occurs, the Lambda function
does not ingest the corresponding data unless the company manually reruns the
job.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure that
the Lambda function ingests all data in the future? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Deploy the Lambda function in multiple Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: Deploying Lambda in multiple AZs does not guarantee reliable processing of messages or retries on failure.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda automates data workflows, processes files, builds scalable web apps, handles IoT requests, and optimizes function performance.

answers.content: Increase the CPU and memory that are allocated to the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Increasing CPU and memory does not address the root cause of network connectivity issues or message loss.

answers.content: Increase provisioned throughput for the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Provisioned throughput is not applicable to Lambda functions and does not resolve message delivery failures.

answers.content: E. Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda automates data workflows, processes files, builds scalable web apps, handles IoT requests, and optimizes function performance.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is developing a VPC architecture that includes multiple
subnets. The architecture will host applications that use Amazon EC2 instances
and Amazon RDS DB instances. The architecture consists of six subnets in two
Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone includes a public subnet, a private
subnet, and a dedicated subnet for databases. Only EC2 instances that run in the
private subnets can have access to the RDS databases.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new route table that excludes the route to the public subnets' CIDR blocks. Associate the route table with the database subnets.
answers.explanation: Route tables control traffic flow but cannot restrict access between specific resources or security groups, so they don't enforce access at the instance level.

answers.content: Create a security group that denies inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the public subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
answers.explanation: Security groups cannot explicitly deny traffic; they are whitelist-based and do not support deny rules, so this approach can't block inbound traffic as intended.

answers.content: Create a security group that allows inbound traffic from the security group that is assigned to instances in the private subnets. Attach the security group to the DB instances.
answers.explanation: Security groups control inbound traffic to resources and are the recommended mechanism to restrict access between layers in a VPC. Assigning a security group to the RDS instances that only allows inbound traffic from EC2 instances in private subnets ensures that only those instances can access the databases. Security groups are stateful and provide fine-grained control without requiring complex routing or peering configurations. Routing and peering solutions are not appropriate to control access at the subnet level for database security.

answers.content: Create a new peering connection between the public subnets and the private subnets. Create a different peering connection between the private subnets and the database subnets.
answers.explanation: VPC peering is for connecting VPCs or subnets across VPCs, and is not needed within the same VPC; it also adds unnecessary complexity compared to security groups.

questions.content:
A company runs an Oracle database on premises. As part of the company's
migration to AWS, the company wants to upgrade the database to the most recent
available version. The company also wants to set up disaster recovery (DR) for
the database. The company needs to minimize the operational overhead for normal
operations and DR setup. The company also needs to maintain access to the
database's underlying operating system.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate the Oracle database to an Amazon EC2 instance. Set up database replication to a different AWS Region.
answers.explanation: Amazon EC2 instances provide access to the underlying operating system, which satisfies the requirement to maintain OS access. Setting up database replication to a different AWS Region supports disaster recovery (DR) with minimized operational overhead. Amazon RDS options do not provide access to the underlying OS, disqualifying them based on the explicit requirement. Migrating to Amazon EC2 allows upgrading to the most recent Oracle version without restrictions imposed by managed services.

answers.content: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Activate Cross-Region automated backups to replicate the snapshots to another AWS Region.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS for Oracle does not provide access to the underlying operating system.

answers.content: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Create a read replica for the database in another AWS Region.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle offers some customization but still does not provide full OS access and may have higher operational overhead.

answers.content: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Create a standby database in another Availability Zone.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS for Oracle standby does not provide OS access and doesn't fully minimize operational overhead for DR setup.

questions.content:
A company has a data ingestion workflow that includes the following components:
An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that receives
notifications about new data deliveries
An AWS Lambda function that processes and stores the data
The ingestion workflow occasionally fails because of network connectivity
issues. When failure occurs, the corresponding data is not ingested unless the
company manually reruns the job.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all notifications are
eventually processed?

answers.content: Configure the Lambda function for deployment across multiple Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: Deployment across multiple Availability Zones does not address message retry and failure handling for SNS notifications.

answers.content: Modify the Lambda function's configuration to increase the CPU and memory allocations for the function.
answers.explanation: Increasing CPU and memory does not guarantee that network connectivity issues or retries are handled properly.

answers.content: Configure the SNS topic's retry strategy to increase both the number of retries and the wait time between retries.
answers.explanation: SNS stops retrying messages and discards them once the retry policy is exhausted unless a dead-letter queue is attached; increasing retries alone is insufficient.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the on-failure destination. Modify the Lambda function to process messages in the queue.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS stops retrying and discards messages when the retry policy is exhausted unless a dead-letter queue is attached. Configuring an Amazon SQS queue as an on-failure destination ensures failed notifications are retained and can be reprocessed. Modifying the Lambda function to process the SQS queue provides a managed retry mechanism and ensures eventual processing of all notifications. This approach aligns with AWS best practices of using managed services for handling retries and failures securely and reliably.

questions.content:
A company has an automobile sales website that stores its listings in a database
on Amazon RDS. When an automobile is sold, the listing needs to be removed from
the website and the data must be sent to multiple target systems.
Which design should a solutions architect recommend?

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for the targets to consume.
answers.explanation: RDS does not natively support triggering Lambda on DB updates; polling or triggers via event notifications are required.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue for the targets to consume.
answers.explanation: Similar to A, lacks fan-out capability which is essential for multiple target systems.

answers.content: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.
answers.explanation: RDS event notifications send messages to SNS, not to SQS queues; incorrect ordering reduces feasibility.

answers.content: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS event notifications can trigger workflows upon database changes. Fan-out through Amazon SNS topics allows notifying multiple targets reliably. Using Amazon SQS queues subscribed to the SNS topic enables decoupling and scaling for each target system. AWS Lambda functions can process notifications from the queues to update each target system appropriately. This approach uses managed AWS services (SNS, SQS, Lambda) designed for event-driven architectures and secure, scalable integrations.

questions.content:
A media company is evaluating the possibility of moving its systems to the AWS
Cloud. The company needs at least 10 TB of storage with the maximum possible I/O
performance for video processing, 300 TB of very durable storage for storing
media content, and 900 TB of storage to meet requirements for archival media
that is not in use anymore.
Which set of services should a solutions architect recommend to meet these
requirements?

answers.content: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS provides maximum possible I/O performance suited for the 10 TB of video processing storage which requires low latency and high throughput. Amazon S3 offers very durable storage for large amounts of media content (300 TB), aligning with durability requirements. Amazon S3 Glacier is the appropriate archival storage solution for 900 TB of media not in use, providing cost-effective long-term storage. This combination leverages managed AWS services optimized for performance, durability, and archival needs.

answers.content: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is not optimal for large-scale durable object storage compared to Amazon S3 for 300 TB media content.

answers.content: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 for archival storage
answers.explanation: Amazon EC2 instance store is ephemeral and not durable, making it unsuitable for persistent maximum performance storage; also, Amazon S3 is better for durable storage than Amazon EFS.

answers.content: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage
answers.explanation: Amazon EC2 instance store lacks durability for maximum performance storage; also, does not meet durability needs well.

questions.content:
A company is migrating its on-premises PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora
PostgreSQL. The on-premises database must remain online and accessible during
the migration. The Aurora database must remain synchronized with the on-premises
database.
Which combination of actions must a solutions architect take to meet these
requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an ongoing replication task.
answers.explanation: CDC start points, checkpoints, loopback prevention, bidirectional replication, premigration assessment auto-execution guide AWS DMS tasks.

answers.content: Create a database backup of the on-premises database.
answers.explanation: Creating a database backup alone does not provide ongoing synchronization and does not keep the databases in sync during migration.

answers.content: Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication server.
answers.explanation: Improving performance when migrating large tables, reducing load on source database, and reducing bottlenecks on target database are key practices covered.

answers.content: Convert the database schema by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT).
answers.explanation: Converting the database schema is important but does not address ongoing synchronization requirements.

answers.content: E. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to monitor the database synchronization.
answers.explanation: Creating an EventBridge rule to monitor synchronization is not a method for ongoing replication or synchronization itself.

questions.content:
A company runs a web-based portal that provides users with global breaking news,
local alerts, and weather updates. The portal delivers each user a personalized
view by using mixture of static and dynamic content. Content is served over
HTTPS through an API server running on an Amazon EC2 instance behind an
Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company wants the portal to provide this
content to its users across the world as quickly as possible.
How should a solutions architect design the application to ensure the LEAST
amount of latency for all users?

answers.content: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve all static and dynamic content by specifying the ALB as an origin.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront improves performance and availability by caching content globally, reducing latency for users worldwide. CloudFront can serve both static and dynamic content from the ALB origin, providing a single point of entry and low-latency delivery. The one-click integration in Elastic Load Balancing console creates a CloudFront distribution with AWS WAF protections, enhancing security. Deploying in a single region with CloudFront leverages global edge locations without the complexity and overhead of multi-region deployments.

answers.content: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.
answers.explanation: Multi-region deployment increases complexity, and Route 53 latency routing does not provide the caching benefits of CloudFront, resulting in higher latency for dynamic and static content.

answers.content: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the static content. Serve the dynamic content directly from the ALB.
answers.explanation: Serving dynamic content directly from ALB without CloudFront can cause higher latency globally; CloudFront can improve performance for both static and dynamic content.

answers.content: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.
answers.explanation: Geolocation routing with multi-region adds operational complexity without caching benefits; CloudFront provides better global low-latency content delivery.

questions.content:
A company's application integrates with multiple software-as-a-service (SaaS)
sources for data collection. The company runs Amazon EC2 instances to receive
the data and to upload the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for analysis. The same
EC2 instance that receives and uploads the data also sends a notification to the
user when an upload is complete. The company has noticed slow application
performance and wants to improve the performance as much as possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group so that EC2 instances can scale out. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.
answers.explanation: While Auto Scaling could improve performance, it still requires EC2 instances to handle data ingestion and notifications, increasing operational overhead compared to managed services.

answers.content: Create an Amazon AppFlow flow to transfer data between each SaaS source and the S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon AppFlow to transfer data between each SaaS source and the S3 bucket offloads data ingestion from EC2 instances, improving performance and reducing operational overhead. Configuring S3 event notifications to trigger SNS notifications upon upload completion fits the requirement to inform users without needing the EC2 instance to send notifications. This solution leverages managed AWS services designed to handle data transfer and notifications with minimal operational management. This aligns with AWS best practices to scale horizontally and use managed services over custom solutions for better performance and lower operational complexity.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for each SaaS source to send output data. Configure the S3 bucket as the rule's target. Create a second EventBridge (Cloud Watch Events) rule to send events when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the second rule's target.
answers.explanation: Using EventBridge rules for each SaaS source and uploads adds complexity and operational overhead compared to a managed data integration service.

answers.content: Create a Docker container to use instead of an EC2 instance. Host the containerized application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights to send events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the upload to the S3 bucket is complete.
answers.explanation: Running containerized workloads on ECS involved refactoring and additional monitoring setup; this does not directly address the data integration bottleneck and adds operational overhead.

questions.content:
A company is running a popular social media website. The website gives users the
ability to upload images to share with other users. The company wants to make
sure that the images do not contain inappropriate content. The company needs a
solution that minimizes development effort.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon Comprehend to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
answers.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service and not designed for image content moderation.

answers.content: Use Amazon Rekognition to detect inappropriate content. Use human review for low-confidence predictions.
answers.explanation: Amazon Rekognition is specifically designed to detect inappropriate, unwanted, or offensive content in images, which aligns directly with the requirement. Rekognition moderation APIs are recommended for social media scenarios to ensure safer user experiences and brand safety. Use of human review for low-confidence predictions is a best practice mentioned to improve accuracy while minimizing errors. This solution minimizes development effort by using a managed service built for this exact purpose.

answers.content: Use Amazon SageMaker to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SageMaker requires building and training custom models, which increases development effort.

answers.content: Use AWS Fargate to deploy a custom machine learning model to detect inappropriate content. Use ground truth to label low-confidence predictions.
answers.explanation: Deploying a custom model on AWS Fargate requires extensive development and operational management, contrary to minimizing effort.

questions.content:
A company wants to run its critical applications in containers to meet
requirements for scalability and availability. The company prefers to focus on
maintenance of the critical applications. The company does not want to be
responsible for provisioning and managing the underlying infrastructure that
runs the containerized workload.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon EC2 instances, and install Docker on the instances.
answers.explanation: Requires managing EC2 instances and Docker, which contradicts the company's preference to avoid infrastructure management.

answers.content: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
answers.explanation: Uses ECS on EC2 worker nodes, requiring provisioning and managing EC2 instances.

answers.content: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate removes the need to provision and manage the underlying infrastructure, allowing the company to focus on maintaining the critical applications. Fargate is a managed service that provides scalability and availability without infrastructure management responsibility. Selecting managed AWS services aligns with best practices over self-managing EC2 instances. This approach supports high availability and scalability as required.

answers.content: Use Amazon EC2 instances from an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)-optimized Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
answers.explanation: Still involves managing EC2 instances even if optimized AMIs are used, which goes against the requirement to avoid infrastructure management.

questions.content:
A company is deploying a new public web application to AWS. The application will
run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application needs to be
encrypted at the edge with an SSL/TLS certificate that is issued by an external
certificate authority (CA). The certificate must be rotated each year before the
certificate expires.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
answers.explanation: Cannot use ACM to issue a certificate from an external CA; it only issues certificates from Amazon’s CA.

answers.content: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an SSL/TLS certificate. Import the key material from the certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALUse the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
answers.explanation: ACM does not support importing key material from certificates it issues; also, it cannot issue external CA certificates.

answers.content: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private Certificate Authority to issue an SSL/TLS certificate from the root CA. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use the managed renewal feature to automatically rotate the certificate.
answers.explanation: ACM Private CA issues private certificates, not valid for public-facing applications, and does not meet the external CA issuance requirement.

answers.content: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to import an SSL/TLS certificate. Apply the certificate to the ALB. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send a notification when the certificate is nearing expiration. Rotate the certificate manually.
answers.explanation: ACM cannot issue certificates from an external CA, so options A, B, and C that rely on ACM issuance do not meet the requirement for using a certificate from an external CA. ACM supports importing external certificates (option D), allowing use of certificates issued by an external CA. Since ACM does not manage renewal for imported certificates, manual rotation is necessary, and sending notifications via EventBridge before expiration supports timely rotation. Security best practices require encrypted connections at the ALB with proper certificate management; D ensures encryption and a process for rotation, balancing security and operational feasibility.

questions.content: A company needs guaranteed Amazon EC2 capacity in three specific Availability\nZones in a specific AWS Region for an upcoming event that will last 1 week.\nWhat should the company do to guarantee the EC2 capacity?

answers.content: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region needed.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances specify only Region for billing discount, do not guarantee capacity.

answers.content: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region needed.
answers.explanation: Capacity Reservation must specify Availability Zones, not just Region, to guarantee capacity.

answers.content: Purchase Reserved Instances that specify the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances do not guarantee capacity in specified Availability Zones.

answers.content: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation that specifies the Region and three Availability Zones needed.
answers.explanation: Capacity Reservations allow you to guarantee EC2 capacity in specific Availability Zones for a duration needed. Option D specifies creating On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the Region and the three Availability Zones, matching the requirement to guarantee capacity in those zones. Reserved Instances do not guarantee capacity in specific Availability Zones, only offer billing discounts for usage. The key facts emphasize use of Capacity Reservations for guaranteed capacity, specifying a Capacity Reservation preference. Security and operational best practices favor using managed AWS services like Capacity Reservations for guaranteed capacity rather than Reserved Instances.

questions.content:
A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must
be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional
9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users,
can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records
must be stored with maximum resiliency.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier is not immediately accessible and lacks Object Lock to guarantee no deletions by root or admin users; access control policies alone are insufficient for enforcing immutable storage.

answers.content: Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
answers.explanation: IAM policies can be changed or overridden and do not provide the guaranteed immutability required; also, Intelligent-Tiering does not fulfill the archival transition requirement.

answers.content: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
answers.explanation: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces a write-once-read-many (WORM) model that prevents anyone, including root and administrative users, from deleting or modifying objects during the retention period. Using an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data after 1 year to Glacier Deep Archive ensures immediate accessibility for the first year with cost-effective archiving for the following 9 years. Storing initially in S3 Standard provides maximum resiliency as required, while Object Lock provides immutable storage for 10 years. Other options do not guarantee immutability for all users or do not use the appropriate durability and data access patterns.

answers.content: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA does not provide maximum resiliency due to single Availability Zone storage, and governance mode Object Lock can be overridden by users with special permissions, so it does not meet the no-deletion requirement.

questions.content:
A company is developing an application that provides order shipping statistics
for retrieval by a REST API. The company wants to extract the shipping
statistics, organize the data into an easy-to-read HTML format, and send the
report to several email addresses at the same time every morning.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these
requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
answers.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is designed for streaming data delivery to destinations such as S3 and is not intended for querying application APIs or sending formatted emails.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
answers.explanation: Amazon SES email receiving configures custom instructions for processing incoming emails via receipt rules, IP address filters. Set up guides, console walkthroughs provided.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Glue jobs are primarily for ETL processes on data in data stores, not for invoking API queries on applications or sending emails via SES.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda automates data workflows, processes files, builds scalable web apps, handles IoT requests, and optimizes function performance.

answers.content: E. Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS as an S3 event destination cannot send formatted email reports; SNS only sends notification messages, not fully formatted HTML email reports.

questions.content:
A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use
Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares
synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company
wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users
currently access the files.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 does not natively support Windows file shares and SMB protocol used by Windows clients.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: S3 File Gateway does not preserve native Windows file share semantics and may introduce compatibility or performance issues.

answers.content: Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed, highly available, and durable storage solution optimized for Windows workloads. FSx for Windows File Server supports the Windows-native Shared Folders experience, preserving how users currently access files. Multi-AZ configuration of FSx offers high availability and durability necessary for critical file share workloads. Amazon S3 and S3 File Gateway do not natively support Windows file share semantics and access methods. Amazon EFS is optimized for Linux-based workloads and does not support Windows SMB protocol natively.

answers.content: Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is designed for Linux workloads and does not provide native SMB support for Windows clients.

questions.content:
A company is developing a two-tier web application on AWS. The company's
developers have deployed the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that connects
directly to a backend Amazon RDS database. The company must not hardcode
database credentials in the application. The company must also implement a
solution to automatically rotate the database credentials on a regular basis.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Store the database credentials in the instance metadata. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and instance metadata at the same time.
answers.explanation: Instance metadata is not designed to store sensitive credentials securely and does not provide managed automatic rotation.

answers.content: Store the database credentials in a configuration file in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to run a scheduled AWS Lambda function that updates the RDS credentials and the credentials in the configuration file at the same time. Use S3 Versioning to ensure the ability to fall back to previous values.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials in an encrypted S3 bucket adds operational complexity and does not inherently support automatic rotation.

answers.content: Store the database credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation for the secret. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the secret.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the preferred managed service for storing and rotating database credentials securely. Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation of credentials, which meets the requirement for regular credential updates without operational overhead. Attaching the appropriate permissions to the EC2 instance role allows secure access to the secrets without hardcoding. This approach follows security best practices by avoiding credentials in code or plaintext storage and leveraging managed services.

answers.content: Store the database credentials as encrypted parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation for the encrypted parameters. Attach the required permission to the EC2 role to grant access to the encrypted parameters.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store does not support automatic rotation, so it cannot fulfill the rotation requirement with minimal operational overhead.

questions.content:
A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application
processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue, writes to an Amazon RDS table, and
deletes the message from the queue. Occasional duplicate records are found in
the RDS table. The SQS queue does not contain any duplicate messages.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure messages are being processed once
only?

answers.content: Use the CreateQueue API call to create a new queue.
answers.explanation: Creating a new queue does not address duplicate processing issues of messages already delivered or being consumed.

answers.content: Use the AddPermission API call to add appropriate permissions.
answers.explanation: Adding permissions does not affect message processing or duplication; it only controls access.

answers.content: Use the ReceiveMessage API call to set an appropriate wait time.
answers.explanation: Setting wait time controls long polling duration but does not prevent duplicate processing of messages.

answers.content: Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.
answers.explanation: Increasing the visibility timeout using ChangeMessageVisibility API call prevents multiple consumers from processing the same message simultaneously, which is a common cause of duplicate records in the database. Since the SQS queue does not deliver duplicate messages, the duplication likely occurs because the message is being processed more than once before it is deleted. Adjusting the visibility timeout is a recommended method to ensure exactly-once processing in distributed consumer applications using SQS.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a
company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly
available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region. The company
needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower traffic if the primary
connection fails.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
answers.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a highly available, consistent low-latency connection to an AWS Region, meeting the primary requirement. Using a VPN connection as a backup ensures failover capability with slower traffic acceptance, aligning with the requirement to minimize costs while providing redundancy. VPNs are managed AWS services that provide secure connectivity and are cost-effective compared to provisioning a second Direct Connect connection. This approach balances security, availability, cost, and operational complexity according to AWS best practices.

answers.content: Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
answers.explanation: VPN connections alone do not provide consistent low latency compared to Direct Connect, which is required for the primary connection.

answers.content: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
answers.explanation: Provisioning two Direct Connect connections is more costly and does not minimize cost as requested.

answers.content: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
answers.explanation: There is no such 'Direct Connect failover attribute' in AWS CLI; automatic backup connections must be provisioned manually or with VPN.

questions.content:
A company is running a business-critical web application on Amazon EC2 instances
behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling
group. The application uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database that is
deployed in a single Availability Zone. The company wants the application to be
highly available with minimum downtime and minimum loss of data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

answers.content: Place the EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks to redirect traffic. Use Aurora PostgreSQL Cross-Region Replication.
answers.explanation: Using multiple AWS Regions and Cross-Region Replication introduces significant complexity and operational overhead, which is not minimal effort.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple Availability Zones. Configure the database as Multi-AZ. Configure an Amazon RDS Proxy instance for the database.
answers.explanation: Configuring the Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones improves availability and fault tolerance for the EC2 instances, aligning with AWS best practices. Configuring the Aurora PostgreSQL database as Multi-AZ provides automated failover with minimal downtime and data loss, ensuring high availability. Using Amazon RDS Proxy enhances database availability by managing connections efficiently and improving failover handling. This solution minimizes operational effort by using managed AWS services for scaling, availability, and database failover.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use one Availability Zone. Generate hourly snapshots of the database. Recover the database from the snapshots in the event of a failure.
answers.explanation: Using only one Availability Zone and relying on hourly snapshots for recovery results in possible data loss and significant downtime, not meeting high availability requirements.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use multiple AWS Regions. Write the data from the application to Amazon S3. Use S3 Event Notifications to launch an AWS Lambda function to write the data to the database.
answers.explanation: Distributing EC2 instances across multiple Regions and writing data indirectly to the database via S3 and Lambda complicates the architecture and increases operational effort.

questions.content:
A company runs a shopping application that uses Amazon DynamoDB to store
customer information. In case of data corruption, a solutions architect needs to
design a solution that meets a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes and
a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour.
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure DynamoDB global tables. For RPO recovery, point the application to a different AWS Region.
answers.explanation: Global tables provide replication but do not directly support point-in-time recovery for corruption scenarios and might not meet the 15-minute RPO.

answers.content: Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB point-in-time recovery (PITR) allows restoring the table to any second in the preceding 35 days, meeting an RPO as low as 15 minutes. Restoring from PITR is a managed service feature, which simplifies recovery and helps meet the RTO of 1 hour. Global tables are for availability and multi-region replication but do not guarantee recovery within a 15-minute RPO without data corruption concerns. Exporting to Glacier daily exceeds the 15-minute RPO due to infrequent backups and slower restore times. EBS snapshots are for EC2 and EBS volumes, not applicable to DynamoDB tables, so cannot be used.

answers.content: Export the DynamoDB data to Amazon S3 Glacier on a daily basis. For RPO recovery, import the data from S3 Glacier to DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Daily export to Glacier is too infrequent to meet the 15-minute RPO and Glacier restore times do not meet the 1-hour RTO requirement.

answers.content: Schedule Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots for the DynamoDB table every 15 minutes. For RPO recovery, restore the DynamoDB table by using the EBS snapshot.
answers.explanation: EBS snapshots cannot be taken of DynamoDB tables, making this approach invalid.

questions.content:
A company runs a photo processing application that needs to frequently upload
and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets that are located in the same AWS
Region. A solutions architect has noticed an increased cost in data transfer
fees and needs to implement a solution to reduce these costs.
How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?

answers.content: Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
answers.explanation: API Gateway is not designed to reduce S3 data transfer costs and adds unnecessary complexity and potential latency.

answers.content: Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway incurs additional data processing charges and does not eliminate internet-bound data transfer costs for S3.

answers.content: Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: Routing through an internet gateway results in internet data transfer charges and potential security risks.

answers.content: Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
answers.explanation: An S3 VPC gateway endpoint allows private connectivity between the VPC and S3 without using an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN connection, or AWS Direct Connect. Using an S3 VPC endpoint eliminates data transfer charges for data transferred between the VPC and S3 within the same Region. It also enhances security by avoiding exposure through the public internet and allows control via endpoint policies. All these points align with reducing data transfer costs and improving security, making it the best solution.

questions.content:
A company recently signed a contract with an AWS Managed Service Provider (MSP)
Partner for help with an application migration initiative. A solutions architect
needs ta share an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from an existing AWS account with
the MSP Partner's AWS account. The AMI is backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store
(Amazon EBS) and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed
key to encrypt EBS volume snapshots.
What is the MOST secure way for the solutions architect to share the AMI with
the MSP Partner's AWS account?

answers.content: Make the encrypted AMI and snapshots publicly available. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
answers.explanation: Making the AMI publicly available creates a security risk by exposing encrypted resources to all accounts.

answers.content: Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key.
answers.explanation: Sharing the AMI via modifying the launchPermission property ensures that only the MSP Partner's AWS account can use the AMI, following the principle of least privilege. Modifying the KMS key policy to allow the MSP Partner's AWS account to use the key is necessary to enable decryption of the encrypted snapshots, which aligns with the requirement that the key must be shared and permission granted for necessary KMS actions. Making the AMI publicly available (option A) violates security best practices by exposing sensitive resources to all AWS accounts. Trusting a new KMS key owned by the MSP Partner (option C) is not feasible for decrypting the snapshots encrypted by the original key without a re-encryption step, which is not described here. Exporting the AMI via S3 (option D) is a complex process not required for sharing AMIs and adds operational overhead compared to native sharing with KMS key permissions.

answers.content: Modify the launchPermission property of the AMI. Share the AMI with the MSP Partner's AWS account only. Modify the key policy to trust a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner for encryption.
answers.explanation: Trusting a new KMS key owned by the MSP Partner does not grant access to the existing encrypted snapshots without proper re-encryption.

answers.content: Export the AMI from the source account to an Amazon S3 bucket in the MSP Partner's AWS account, Encrypt the S3 bucket with a new KMS key that is owned by the MSP Partner. Copy and launch the AMI in the MSP Partner's AWS account.
answers.explanation: Exporting and copying the AMI via S3 is an unnecessary manual step and less secure than sharing with launch permissions and key access.

questions.content:
A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a
private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance
in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the
on-premises network, through the company's internet connection, to the bastion
host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure
that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access.
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these
requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
answers.explanation: Allows inbound access from application instances to bastion host, which is the opposite of the required connection flow.

answers.content: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
answers.explanation: Allows inbound access from internal IP range, but connection is from on-premises via company's internet, so external IP range is needed.

answers.content: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
answers.explanation: Configure security group rules for EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, target instances, allow traffic between endpoint and instances, specify source/destination security groups or IP ranges, client IP preservation affects source IP.

answers.content: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
answers.explanation: EKS clusters require specific security group rules controlling control plane-node communication ports traffic.

answers.content: E. Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.
answers.explanation: Allows inbound SSH access from public IP of bastion host, which is less secure than using the private IP within the VPC.

questions.content:
A company hosts its web applications in the AWS Cloud. The company configures
Elastic Load Balancers to use certificates that are imported into AWS
Certificate Manager (ACM). The company's security team must be notified 30 days
before the expiration of each certificate.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

answers.content: Add a rule in ACM to publish a custom message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic every day, beginning 30 days before any certificate will expire.
answers.explanation: ACM does not support adding rules to publish custom messages for certificate expiration.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule that checks for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) when AWS Config reports a noncompliant resource.
answers.explanation: AWS Config can evaluate compliance of ACM certificates and check if certificates will expire within a specified timeframe. Amazon EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) can respond to AWS Config's noncompliance by triggering notifications via Amazon SNS. This approach uses managed AWS services for automated compliance checking and alerting, aligning with security best practices for timely notifications. Other options either rely on unsupported features (ACM rules), do not provide direct monitoring for expiration within 30 days, or require custom code rather than managed services.

answers.content: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for certificates that will expire within 30 days. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on Trusted Advisor metrics for check status changes. Configure the alarm to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor does not provide metrics directly supporting monitoring of certificate expiration or triggering CloudWatch alarms.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule to detect any certificates that will expire within 30 days. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to send a custom alert by way of Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
answers.explanation: There is no native EventBridge rule that detects certificate expiration; this requires custom periodic polling which is less preferred than managed compliance checks.

questions.content:
A company needs to store data in Amazon S3 and must prevent the data from being
changed. The company wants new objects that are uploaded to Amazon S3 to remain
unchangeable for a nonspecific amount of time until the company decides to
modify the objects. Only specific users in the company's AWS account can have
the ability 10 delete the objects.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an S3 Glacier vault. Apply a write-once, read-many (WORM) vault lock policy to the objects.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier vault lock applies to archives, not S3 objects, and does not provide the needed object-level control.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Set a retention period of 100 years. Use governance mode as the S3 bucket's default retention mode for new objects.
answers.explanation: Governance mode allows users with special permissions to override retention, reducing strict immutability; also the retention period is fixed at 100 years, whereas the requirement is nonspecific.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket. Use AWS CloudTrail to track any S3 API events that modify the objects. Upon notification, restore the modified objects from any backup versions that the company has.
answers.explanation: Using CloudTrail and backup is reactive and does not prevent object modification, which violates the immutability requirement.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock enabled. Enable versioning. Add a legal hold to the objects. Add the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission to the IAM policies of users who need to delete the objects.
answers.explanation: S3 Object Lock with versioning enabled allows objects to be protected from modification or deletion. A legal hold can be placed on objects without a fixed retention period, aligning with the nonspecific time requirement. The s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission controls which users can place or remove legal holds, ensuring only specific users can delete objects. This approach uses managed AWS services and security best practices to enforce immutability and fine-grained access control.

questions.content:
A company wants to reduce the cost of its existing three-tier web architecture.
The web, application, and database servers are running on Amazon EC2 instances
for the development, test, and production environments. The EC2 instances
average 30% CPU utilization during peak hours and 10% CPU utilization during
non-peak hours.
The production EC2 instances run 24 hours a day. The development and test EC2
instances run for at least 8 hours each day. The company plans to implement
automation to stop the development and test EC2 instances when they are not in
use.
Which EC2 instance purchasing solution will meet the company's requirements MOST
cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use Spot Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Spot Instances are not recommended for production as they can be interrupted and cause instability in a 24/7 production environment.

answers.content: Use Reserved Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances provide cost savings and predictability for production environments running 24/7, which suits the production EC2 instances with steady usage. On-Demand Instances offer flexibility and are suitable for development and test environments that run part-time and can be stopped when not in use, aligning with the company's plan for automation to stop these instances. Spot Instances and Spot blocks are less suitable for production due to their possible interruptions, which is not ideal for a continuously running production tier.

answers.content: Use Spot blocks for the production EC2 instances. Use Reserved Instances for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Spot blocks are fixed duration Spot Instances and may not provide the reliability needed for production running 24/7.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances for the production EC2 instances. Use Spot blocks for the development and test EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Instances for production miss potential cost savings from Reserved Instances; Spot blocks for dev/test risk interruption.

questions.content:
A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. One of the
applications needs to call the Amazon S3 API to store and read objects.
According to the company's security regulations, no traffic from the
applications is allowed to travel across the internet.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: Configuring an S3 gateway endpoint enables private connectivity between EC2 instances and Amazon S3 without traffic crossing the internet. An S3 gateway endpoint integrates with the VPC routing to keep S3 API calls within the AWS network, complying with the security regulation of no internet traffic. This approach is aligned with AWS best practices to use managed VPC endpoints for secure, private access to AWS services.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket in a private subnet.
answers.explanation: You cannot create an S3 bucket in a private subnet; S3 is a regional service, not deployed inside VPC subnets.

answers.content: Create an S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Having the S3 bucket in the same region does not prevent traffic from traveling over the internet unless using a private endpoint.

answers.content: Configure a NAT gateway in the same subnet as the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway routes traffic through the internet and does not meet the security requirement of no internet traffic.

questions.content:
A company runs an on-premises application that is powered by a MySQL database.
The company is migrating the application to AWS to increase the application's
elasticity and availability.
The current architecture shows heavy read activity on the database during times
of normal operation. Every 4 hours, the company's development team pulls a full
export of the production database to populate a database in the staging
environment. During this period, users experience unacceptable application
latency. The development team is unable to use the staging environment until the
procedure completes.
A solutions architect must recommend replacement architecture that alleviates
the application latency issue. The replacement architecture also must give the
development team the ability to continue using the staging environment without
delay.
Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.
answers.explanation: Using mysqldump backup and restore causes lengthy downtime and latency periods not suitable for heavy production environments.

answers.content: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Use database cloning to create the staging database on-demand.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora MySQL supports database cloning which allows instant, space-efficient copies of the production database for staging environments. Using Aurora cloning enables development teams to access a fresh staging database without impacting production performance or causing latency. Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas increase availability and elasticity for the production database with read scaling, addressing the heavy read workload. Backup and restore processes involving mysqldump are time-consuming and induce latency during dump and restore operations, which violates the requirement to avoid unacceptable application latency. RDS Multi-AZ deployments use a standby for failover, not for staging environments, and read replicas are not suitable as staging DBs because they are read-only.

answers.content: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Use the standby instance for the staging database.
answers.explanation: The standby instance in a Multi-AZ deployment is passive and cannot be used as a staging database; it’s not accessible for reads or writes.

answers.content: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.
answers.explanation: Using mysqldump and restore with RDS MySQL will cause delays and does not provide on-demand staging environments.

questions.content:
A company's HTTP application is behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB's
target group is configured to use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with multiple
EC2 instances that run the web service.
The company notices that the NLB is not detecting HTTP errors for the
application. These errors require a manual restart of the EC2 instances that run
the web service. The company needs to improve the application's availability
without writing custom scripts or code.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Enable HTTP health checks on the NLB, supplying the URL of the company's application.
