On-Demand Instances provide stable compute capacity without interruptions, fitting a stateless batch processing job that can be stopped and started without impact. Reserved Instances are less flexible and not ideal for highly dynamic workloads. AWS Lambda is not suitable for long-running tasks typically taking more than 15 minutes maximum invocation time. Spot Instances are cost-effective but risky for jobs longer than one hour due to possible interruptions.

answers.content: Implement the processing on AWS Lambda.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda has a maximum execution time limit of 15 minutes, unsuitable for jobs taking over 60 minutes.

questions.content:
A company uses a three-tier web application to provide training to new
employees. The application is accessed for only 12 hours every day. The company
is using an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance to store information and wants to
minimize costs.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure an IAM policy for AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Create an IAM role for the policy. Update the trust relationship of the role. Set up automatic start and stop for the DB instance.
answers.explanation: This option mixes unrelated IAM and Systems Manager configurations and does not directly address automatic start/stop of the DB instance.

answers.content: Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache cluster that gives users the ability to access the data from the cache when the DB instance is stopped. Invalidate the cache after the DB instance is started.
answers.explanation: Using ElastiCache to access data when the RDS instance is stopped is not feasible because cache cannot fully replace the database, and the DB must be running for writes; also, this adds unnecessary complexity and cost.

answers.content: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Create an IAM role that grants access to Amazon RDS. Attach the role to the EC2 instance. Configure a cron job to start and stop the EC2 instance on the desired schedule.
answers.explanation: Starting and stopping an EC2 instance is irrelevant here because the goal is to minimize costs related to the RDS DB instance, not EC2; it also adds operational overhead by managing EC2.

answers.content: Create AWS Lambda functions to start and stop the DB instance. Create Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled rules to invoke the Lambda functions. Configure the Lambda functions as event targets for the rules.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Lambda functions with Amazon EventBridge scheduled rules to start and stop the RDS instance is a managed, secure, and cost-effective solution to run the database only during the required 12 hours. This method automates the process without requiring manual intervention or additional infrastructure, aligning with best practices to minimize operational overhead. It avoids maintaining extra resources like EC2 instances or caching solutions that add complexity or cost. Controlling RDS instance runtime directly reduces unnecessary cost while maintaining security by leveraging AWS managed services.

questions.content:
A solutions architect needs to help a company optimize the cost of running an
application on AWS. The application will use Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Fargate,
and AWS Lambda for compute within the architecture.
The EC2 instances will run the data ingestion layer of the application. EC2
usage will be sporadic and unpredictable. Workloads that run on EC2 instances
can be interrupted at any time. The application front end will run on Fargate,
and Lambda will serve the API layer. The front-end utilization and API layer
utilization will be predictable over the course of the next year.
Which combination of purchasing options will provide the MOST cost-effective
solution for hosting this application? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer
answers.explanation: AWS Batch optimizes EC2 Spot instances, reducing costs. Configure job retries, instance types, allocation strategy. Monitor Spot Interruption Dashboard.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances for the data ingestion layer
answers.explanation: On-Demand Instances are more expensive and not optimal for sporadic, interruptible workloads compared to Spot Instances.

answers.content: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
answers.explanation: Guidance on how to optimize spending for Windows on Amazon EC2 by using Savings Plans.

answers.content: Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved instances for the data ingestion layer.
answers.explanation: 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances are not suitable for unpredictable and interruptible EC2 workloads and lack flexibility.

answers.content: E. Purchase a 1-year EC2 instance Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
answers.explanation: An EC2-only Savings Plan is less flexible than a Compute Savings Plan, which covers both Fargate and Lambda compute costs.

questions.content:
A company wants to move a multi-tiered application from on premises to the AWS
Cloud to improve the application's performance. The application consists of
application tiers that communicate with each other by way of RESTful services.
Transactions are dropped when one tier becomes overloaded. A solutions architect
must design a solution that resolves these issues and modernizes the
application.
Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

answers.content: Use Amazon API Gateway and direct transactions to the AWS Lambda functions as the application layer. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) as the communication layer between application services.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions as the application layer modernizes the application into a serverless architecture, improving operational efficiency by removing the need to manage servers. Using Amazon SQS between services decouples the application tiers, allowing messages to be reliably queued and processed asynchronously to prevent transaction drops during overload. This design improves application performance by smoothing traffic spikes and scaling automatically without manual intervention. It aligns with AWS best practices favoring managed services for scalability, reliability, and operational efficiency.

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to analyze the application performance history to determine the servers' peak utilization during the performance failures. Increase the size of the application server's Amazon EC2 instances to meet the peak requirements.
answers.explanation: Scaling EC2 instances manually to peak utilization is less operationally efficient and does not prevent dropped transactions during overload.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SNS queue length and scale up and down as required.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS is a pub/sub messaging service not designed for queueing or handling backpressure, so it cannot reliably buffer transactions during overload.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to handle the messaging between application servers running on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group. Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the SQS queue length and scale up when communication failures are detected.
answers.explanation: While SQS is appropriate for queueing, using EC2 instances instead of Lambda increases management overhead and reduces operational efficiency compared to a serverless approach.

questions.content:
A company needs to save the results from a medical trial to an Amazon S3
repository. The repository must allow a few scientists to add new files and must
restrict all other users to read-only access. No users can have the ability to
modify or delete any files in the repository. The company must keep every file
in the repository for a minimum of 1 year after its creation date.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode with a legal hold of 1 year.
answers.explanation: Governance mode allows privileged users to alter or delete objects, which does not meet the strict no-modification requirement.

answers.content: Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days.
answers.explanation: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode enforces a retention period that prevents any user from deleting or modifying objects until the retention period expires. Setting a retention period of 365 days meets the requirement of keeping every file for at least one year after creation. Compliance mode is stricter than governance mode, ensuring no users can modify or delete objects, which aligns with the requirement. IAM roles and bucket policies alone cannot reliably prevent modifications or deletions because users with sufficient permissions can override these policies. Automated Lambda functions and hash tracking do not prevent deletions or modifications inherently and add unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Use an IAM role to restrict all users from deleting or changing objects in the S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to only allow the IAM role.
answers.explanation: IAM roles and bucket policies can be overridden by administrators or users with sufficient privileges, thus cannot guarantee no modifications or deletions.

answers.content: Configure the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function every time an object is added. Configure the function to track the hash of the saved object so that modified objects can be marked accordingly.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda to track hashes does not prevent modifications or deletions, failing to meet the strict retention requirements.

questions.content:
A global company is using Amazon API Gateway to design REST APIs for its loyalty
club users in the us-east-1 Region and the ap-southeast-2 Region. A solutions
architect must design a solution to protect these API Gateway managed REST APIs
across multiple accounts from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of
administrative effort?

answers.content: Set up AWS WAF in both Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
answers.explanation: Requires managing AWS WAF web ACLs separately in each Region and account, increasing administrative effort.

answers.content: Set up AWS Firewall Manager in both Regions. Centrally configure AWS WAF rules.
answers.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager allows centralized management and configuration of AWS WAF rules across multiple accounts and Regions, reducing administrative overhead. Setting up Firewall Manager in both Regions supports managing protections for API Gateway APIs across multiple accounts efficiently. AWS WAF is the appropriate service to protect against SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks, and Firewall Manager simplifies its deployment and maintenance at scale.

answers.content: Set up AWS Shield in bath Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield provides DDoS protection, not specifically protection against SQL injection or cross-site scripting attacks.

answers.content: Set up AWS Shield in one of the Regions. Associate Regional web ACLs with an API stage.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield in one Region does not cover multiple Regions nor provides protection against the specified web exploits.

questions.content:
An Amazon EC2 administrator created the following policy associated with an IAM
group containing several users:
[https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-associate-saa-c03/image1.png]
What is the effect of this policy?

answers.content: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in any AWS Region except us-east-1.
answers.explanation: The policy allows the ec2:TerminateInstances action with a Condition that the aws:RequestedRegion is not us-east-1. This means users can terminate EC2 instances in all regions except us-east-1. No condition restricts termination by source IP, so IP address conditions do not affect this policy. IAM policies evaluate conditions specified; here, the condition excludes the us-east-1 region from permission.

answers.content: Users can terminate an EC2 instance with the IP address 10.100.100.1 in the us-east-1 Region.
answers.explanation: Policy does not specify IP address conditions affecting instance termination permissions.

answers.content: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.
answers.explanation: Source IP condition is not present in the policy, so no IP-based allow applies.

answers.content: Users cannot terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the user's source IP is 10.100.100.254.
answers.explanation: Policy does not explicitly deny termination from any source IP; the condition is on region only.

questions.content:
A social media company allows users to upload images to its website. The website
runs on Amazon EC2 instances. During upload requests, the website resizes the
images to a standard size and stores the resized images in Amazon S3. Users are
experiencing slow upload requests to the website.
The company needs to reduce coupling within the application and improve website
performance. A solutions architect must design the most operationally efficient
process for image uploads.
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these
requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure the application to upload images to S3 Glacier.
answers.explanation: Uploading to S3 Glacier is unsuitable for images needing quick access and resizing, as Glacier is designed for archival storage with high retrieval latency.

answers.content: Configure the web server to upload the original images to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Having the web server upload original images to S3 does not reduce the coupling nor address performance issues since uploads still go through the web server.

answers.content: Configure the application to upload images directly from each user's browser to Amazon S3 through the use of a presigned URL
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 enables storing, retrieving data from EC2 instances, copying files between S3, EC2, synchronizing buckets with local directories, accessing data via APIs, SDKs for data lakes, backups.

answers.content: Configure S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when an image is uploaded. Use the function to resize the image.
answers.explanation: Process Amazon EC2 lifecycle events with Lambda functions invoked by EventBridge, configured to forward events like instance state changes or EBS snapshots.

answers.content: E. Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function on a schedule to resize uploaded images.
answers.explanation: Using scheduled Lambda invocations via EventBridge is less efficient and responsive than event-driven resizing triggered immediately upon upload.

questions.content:
A company wants to migrate its existing on-premises monolithic application to
AWS. The company wants to keep as much of the front-end code and the backend
code as possible. However, the company wants to break the application into
smaller applications. A different team will manage each application. The company
needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Host the application on AWS Lambda. Integrate the application with Amazon API Gateway.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda is suitable for event-driven architectures but may require significant application refactoring and is not ideal for migrating monolithic applications with minimal code changes.

answers.content: Host the application with AWS Amplify. Connect the application to an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with AWS Lambda.
answers.explanation: AWS Amplify is primarily focused on front-end and mobile applications and does not naturally support backend application segmentation and scalability needed here.

answers.content: Host the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Set up an Application Load Balancer with EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group as targets.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances with load balancers requires more operational overhead compared to managed container services like ECS.

answers.content: Host the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up an Application Load Balancer with Amazon ECS as the target.
answers.explanation: Amazon ECS supports containerizing existing applications with AWS App2Container, enabling migration without code changes and better workload segmentation. ECS with an Application Load Balancer and Auto Scaling provides high scalability and reduces operational overhead. Breaking the monolithic application into smaller containerized applications aligns with managing multiple teams each responsible for different applications. AWS managed container services are preferred for operational efficiency and scalability over manually managing EC2 instances.

questions.content:
A company hosts a website analytics application on a single Amazon EC2 On-Demand
Instance. The analytics software is written in PHP and uses a MySQL database.
The analytics software, the web server that provides PHP, and the database
server are all hosted on the EC2 instance. The application is showing signs of
performance degradation during busy times and is presenting 5xx errors. The
company needs to make the application scale seamlessly.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the load to each EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Does not provide automatic scaling or load balancing beyond two fixed instances; less cost-effective and less scalable than an Auto Scaling group.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Use the AMI to launch a second EC2 On-Demand Instance. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to distribute the load across the two EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Route 53 weighted routing is not suitable for real-time load balancing or scaling; does not handle instance health or automatic scaling.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AWS Lambda function to stop the EC2 instance and change the instance type. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function when CPU utilization surpasses 75%.
answers.explanation: Scaling by changing instance type manually via Lambda and CloudWatch alarm is not seamless scaling and introduces downtime; also does not involve load balancing.

answers.content: Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance. Create an AMI of the web application. Apply the AMI to a launch template. Create an Auto Scaling group with the launch template Configure the launch template to use a Spot Fleet. Attach an Application Load Balancer to the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Migrating the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL provides a managed, scalable, and highly available database service optimized for performance, which is important for scaling applications. Using an Auto Scaling group with a launch template allows the web application to scale out seamlessly during busy times, meeting the scalability requirement. Applying the AMI to a launch template ensures consistent configuration of EC2 instances. Attaching an Application Load Balancer distributes incoming traffic effectively across instances, improving performance and fault tolerance. Using a Spot Fleet within the launch template's Auto Scaling group provides a cost-effective instance purchasing option. This solution uses managed AWS services and follows best practices for scalability and cost-effectiveness.

questions.content:
A company wants to migrate its on-premises data center to AWS. According to the
company's compliance requirements, the company can use only the ap-northeast-3
Region. Company administrators are not permitted to connect VPCs to the
internet.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use AWS Control Tower to implement data residency guardrails to deny internet access and deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower functionality varies across Regions due to regional availability of underlying services like AWS Service Catalog, Account Factory Customizations, and IAM Identity Center. Controls are deployable only in Regions with required dependencies, impacting governed Regions.

answers.content: Use rules in AWS WAF to prevent internet access. Deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3 in the AWS account settings.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF is designed to protect web applications and is not used to prevent VPC internet access; denying Regions in account settings alone is insufficient.

answers.content: Use AWS Organizations to configure service control policies (SCPS) that prevent VPCs from gaining internet access. Deny access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-3.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations spans commercial, GovCloud, China Regions; China accounts require separate organization setup.

answers.content: Create an outbound rule for the network ACL in each VPC to deny all traffic from 0.0.0.0/0. Create an IAM policy for each user to prevent the use of any AWS Region other than ap-northeast-3.
answers.explanation: Network ACL outbound rules deny traffic but do not prevent VPC internet gateway configuration, and IAM policies cannot enforce region restrictions globally for all resources effectively.

answers.content: E. Use AWS Config to activate managed rules to detect and alert for internet gateways and to detect and alert for new resources deployed outside of ap-northeast-3.
answers.explanation: AWS Config managed rules only detect and alert rather than prevent internet access or cross-region usage, which does not meet the requirement to block these.

questions.content:
A company is building a web-based application running on Amazon EC2 instances in
multiple Availability Zones. The web application will provide access to a
repository of text documents totaling about 900 TB in size. The company
anticipates that the web application will experience periods of high demand. A
solutions architect must ensure that the storage component for the text
documents can scale to meet the demand of the application at all times. The
company is concerned about the overall cost of the solution.
Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS is not cost-effective or scalable for hundreds of terabytes and multiple AZs.

answers.content: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is more expensive at this scale and not optimized for very large datasets like 900 TB.

answers.content: Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
answers.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service is intended for search and analytics, not for cost-effective large-scale document storage.

answers.content: Amazon S3
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 can scale to store extremely large amounts of data, including hundreds of terabytes, without provisioning storage upfront. S3 provides cost-effective storage compared to block or file storage services, especially at large scale. S3 supports multiple Availability Zones natively, offering high availability and durability. Amazon EBS and EFS are generally more costly and less scalable for very large datasets like 900 TB. Using S3 aligns with the provided facts indicating bulk document uploads and processing are integrated with S3.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is designing the cloud architecture for a new application
being deployed on AWS. The process should run in parallel while adding and
removing application nodes as needed based on the number of jobs to be
processed. The processor application is stateless. The solutions architect must
ensure that the application is loosely coupled and the job items are durably
stored.
Which design should the solutions architect use?

answers.content: Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on CPU usage.
answers.explanation: SNS does not durably store messages and does not provide inherent queueing for job processing, so it is not loosely coupled or durable.

answers.content: Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch configuration that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch configuration. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on network usage.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling based on network usage is not an effective metric for scaling based on job queue length; also, a launch configuration is older than launch templates.

answers.content: Create an Amazon SQS queue to hold the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of items in the SQS queue.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS durably stores jobs ensuring loose coupling between application nodes and the process generating jobs. Using a launch template is a modern best practice for Auto Scaling group creation over launch configurations. Setting the Auto Scaling policy based on the number of items in the SQS queue allows scaling the processor application according to workload demand, meeting the need for parallel processing and dynamic node management. This approach aligns with AWS best practices favoring durable queues for decoupling and scalable, event-driven architectures.

answers.content: Create an Amazon SNS topic to send the jobs that need to be processed. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that consists of the processor application. Create a launch template that uses the AMI. Create an Auto Scaling group using the launch template. Set the scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to add and remove nodes based on the number of messages published to the SNS topic.
answers.explanation: SNS topic scaling based on message publications does not reflect actual processing load and SNS does not queue messages durably for worker nodes.

questions.content:
A company has a large Microsoft SharePoint deployment running on-premises that
requires Microsoft Windows shared file storage. The company wants to migrate
this workload to the AWS Cloud and is considering various storage options. The
storage solution must be highly available and integrated with Active Directory
for access control.
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

answers.content: Configure Amazon EFS storage and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS does not natively support SMB protocol or direct integration with Microsoft Active Directory for authentication.

answers.content: Create an SMB file share on an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in two Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway does not provide native Active Directory integration and is primarily designed for hybrid cloud backup and caching rather than fully managed SMB shares.

answers.content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket and configure Microsoft Windows Server to mount it as a volume.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 buckets cannot be mounted natively as SMB shares for Windows file systems and do not support Active Directory integration.

answers.content: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS and set the Active Directory domain for authentication.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a managed AWS service that provides fully managed native Microsoft Windows shared file storage. It integrates directly with Active Directory for access control, meeting the requirement for AD authentication. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is designed for high availability and seamless integration with Windows applications such as SharePoint.

questions.content:
A company's website provides users with downloadable historical performance
reports. The website needs a solution that will scale to meet the company's
website demands globally. The solution should be cost-effective, limit the
provisioning of infrastructure resources, and provide the fastest possible
response time.
Which combination should a solutions architect recommend to meet these
requirements?

answers.content: Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network that caches content at edge locations, providing the fastest response time for users worldwide. Amazon S3 provides a cost-effective, scalable, and durable storage solution to host static files like historical performance reports without needing to provision infrastructure. Combining CloudFront with S3 meets the requirement to scale globally, reduce costs by offloading requests to edge caches, and minimize infrastructure provisioning.

answers.content: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda and DynamoDB do not provide the fastest response for downloadable static files and introduce unnecessary compute and database complexity.

answers.content: Application Load Balancer with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancer with EC2 Auto Scaling requires provisioning and managing infrastructure, which is less cost-effective and scalable compared to CloudFront and S3 for static content.

answers.content: Amazon Route 53 with internal Application Load Balancers
answers.explanation: Route 53 with internal ALBs is not suitable for global content delivery and involves managing infrastructure without caching benefits.

questions.content:
A company is running a multi-tier web application on premises. The web
application is containerized and runs on a number of Linux hosts connected to a
PostgreSQL database that contains user records. The operational overhead of
maintaining the infrastructure and capacity planning is limiting the company's
growth. A solutions architect must improve the application's infrastructure.
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish
this? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to Amazon Aurora.
answers.explanation: Aurora managed relational database offers MySQL PostgreSQL compatibility, automated clustering, replication, scalable storage subsystem.

answers.content: Migrate the web application to be hosted on Amazon EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Hosting on Amazon EC2 still requires management of servers and capacity planning, not reducing operational overhead effectively.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the web application content.
answers.explanation: CloudFront primarily caches content and improves global delivery but does not address infrastructure management or application hosting and database scalability.

answers.content: Set up Amazon ElastiCache between the web application and the PostgreSQL database.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache introduces caching but does not address the core issue of operational overhead; it adds complexity rather than reducing infrastructure maintenance.

answers.content: E. Migrate the web application to be hosted on AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
answers.explanation: Provides detailed information and instructions on getting started and working with AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS.

questions.content:
An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zonas.
The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load
Balancer. The application performs best when the CPU utilization of the EC2
instances is at or near 40%.
What should a solutions architect do to maintain the desired performance across
all instances in the group?

answers.content: Use a simple scaling policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Simple scaling policies are not recommended due to manual cooldown management and less adaptive scaling.

answers.content: Use a target tracking policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Target tracking scaling policies dynamically adjust the Auto Scaling group to maintain the metric (CPU utilization) near the target value, here 40%. AWS best practices recommend target tracking policies over simple scaling because they provide proportional and automatic scaling without the need to manage cooldowns manually. Scheduled scaling and Lambda functions do not adapt to changing CPU utilization dynamically, risking performance degradation or resource wastage. Simple scaling is less recommended by AWS and requires cooldown management, making it less effective and more manual.

answers.content: Use an AWS Lambda function ta update the desired Auto Scaling group capacity.
answers.explanation: Using Lambda to update capacity is manual and does not provide automatic dynamic scaling based on CPU utilization.

answers.content: Use scheduled scaling actions to scale up and scale down the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Scheduled scaling is not responsive to real-time CPU utilization, which can lead to suboptimal performance.

questions.content:
A gaming company is designing a highly available architecture. The application
runs on a modified Linux kernel and supports only UDP-based traffic. The company
needs the front-end tier to provide the best possible user experience. That tier
must have low latency, route traffic to the nearest edge location, and provide
static IP addresses for entry into the application endpoints.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure Amazon Route 53 to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in AWS Application Auto Scaling.
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancer does not support UDP traffic.

answers.content: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in an AWS Application Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: CloudFront is primarily for HTTP/HTTPS traffic and does not provide static IP addresses or support UDP natively.

answers.content: Configure AWS Global Accelerator to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses and routes traffic to the nearest edge location, meeting low latency and nearest edge requirements. Global Accelerator forwards traffic to Network Load Balancer which supports UDP traffic and provides high availability. Using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group aligns with managing the application on a modified Linux kernel. Other options use Application Load Balancers or API Gateway that do not support UDP, or do not provide static IPs and global edge routing as effectively.

answers.content: Configure Amazon API Gateway to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: API Gateway and Application Load Balancer do not support UDP traffic and do not provide static IPs.

questions.content:
A company is designing an application where users upload small files into Amazon
S3. After a user uploads a file, the file requires one-time simple processing to
transform the data and save the data in JSON format for later analysis.
Each file must be processed as quickly as possible after it is uploaded. Demand
will vary. On some days, users will upload a high number of files. On other
days, users will upload a few files or no files.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Configure Amazon EMR to read text files from Amazon S3. Run processing scripts to transform the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
answers.explanation: Amazon EMR and Aurora involve more operational overhead and are less suitable for varied, sporadic demand with quick processing.

answers.content: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances requires managing servers and scaling manually, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon S3 event notifications with Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda minimizes operational overhead by leveraging serverless compute and managed messaging services. AWS Lambda scales automatically with demand, ensuring quick processing without manual intervention. Storing the processed data in Amazon DynamoDB is appropriate for JSON and provides managed database services with minimal maintenance. This solution aligns with AWS best practices prioritizing managed services and low operational burdens.

answers.content: Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams when a new file is uploaded. Use an AWS Lambda function to consume the event from the stream and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
answers.explanation: Using EventBridge and Kinesis Data Streams adds unnecessary complexity instead of directly using SQS and Lambda which better fit the use case.

questions.content:
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to reduce a company's
storage costs. All the company's data is in the Amazon S3 Standard storage
class. The company must keep all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most
recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
answers.explanation: Transitioning data immediately to Glacier Deep Archive fails the requirement for the most recent 2 years of highly available and immediately retrievable data.

answers.content: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
answers.explanation: The data must be highly available and immediately retrievable for the most recent 2 years, so data for that period should remain in the S3 Standard storage class. After 2 years, data can be transitioned to a lower-cost storage class such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term retention of 25 years. An S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years aligns with both cost reduction and availability requirements. Using a lifecycle policy is a managed AWS service recommended for lifecycle management and cost optimization.

answers.content: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archiving transitions may not guarantee immediate retrieval and is designed for unpredictable access patterns, not strict 2-year access requirements.

answers.content: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
answers.explanation: Transitioning immediately to One Zone-IA risks data availability in case of AZ failure and conflicts with the requirement for immediate availability for recent data.

questions.content:
A company runs a stateless web application in production on a group of Amazon
EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application
experiences heavy usage during an 8-hour period each business day. Application
usage is moderate and steady overnight. Application usage is low during
weekends.
The company wants to minimize its EC2 costs without affecting the availability
of the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use Spot Instances for the entire workload.
answers.explanation: Using Spot Instances for the entire workload risks availability due to potential interruptions and is not suitable for baseline capacity.

answers.content: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
answers.explanation: Reserved Instances are less flexible and less cost-effective for variable workloads; On-Demand Instances provide better flexibility for baseline usage.

answers.content: Use On-Demand Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
answers.explanation: Using On-Demand Instances for the baseline usage ensures stable and reliable capacity during heavy and moderate periods. Adding Spot Instances for additional capacity leverages cost savings when usage spikes without affecting baseline availability. Spot Instances are suitable for scaling additional capacity due to their lower cost and because the application is stateless. Reserved or Dedicated Instances are less flexible for fluctuating workloads, and using Spot Instances exclusively risks availability loss.

answers.content: Use Dedicated Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use On-Demand Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
answers.explanation: Dedicated Instances increase costs unnecessarily and do not provide cost savings for fluctuating workloads.

questions.content:
A company recently started using Amazon Aurora as the data store for its global
ecommerce application. When large reports are run, developers report that the
ecommerce application is performing poorly. After reviewing metrics in Amazon
CloudWatch, a solutions architect finds that the ReadIOPS and CPUUtilizalion
metrics are spiking when monthly reports run.
What is the MOST cost-effective solution?

answers.content: Migrate the monthly reporting to Amazon Redshift.
answers.explanation: Redshift is a different service and adding complexity and cost; not the most cost-effective solution.

answers.content: Migrate the monthly reporting to an Aurora Replica.
answers.explanation: Migrating the monthly reporting to an Aurora Replica is the most cost-effective way to reduce load on the primary instance and improve read performance. Using Aurora Replicas to scale reads is a recommended best practice for improving performance and scalability of Aurora MySQL clusters. Increasing Provisioned IOPS or moving to a larger instance can be more costly and may not address read scaling effectively. Migrating to Redshift might improve reporting but is a different service designed for data warehousing, which adds complexity and cost. The use of T instance classes is only recommended for non-production workloads, so upgrading the instance class should be considered carefully.

answers.content: Migrate the Aurora database to a larger instance class.
answers.explanation: Upgrading to a larger instance increases cost without addressing read scalability or reducing IOPS spikes efficiently.

answers.content: Increase the Provisioned IOPS on the Aurora instance.
answers.explanation: Increasing Provisioned IOPS raises cost and does not scale reads as effectively as adding an Aurora Replica.

questions.content:
A company has a service that produces event data. The company wants to use AWS
to process the event data as it is received. The data is written in a specific
order that must be maintained throughout processing. The company wants to
implement a solution that minimizes operational overhead.
How should a solutions architect accomplish this?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue to hold messages. Set up an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the queue.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS FIFO queues maintain the specific order of messages, which is required by the question. Using AWS Lambda with SQS FIFO minimizes operational overhead by providing a managed event-driven processing solution. Amazon SNS does not guarantee message ordering, so its options are unsuitable where ordered processing is required. Standard SQS queues do not guarantee order, so they do not meet the requirement. Leveraging managed services like SQS FIFO and Lambda aligns with AWS best practices for scalable, ordered, and low-overhead processing.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to deliver notifications containing payloads to process. Configure an AWS Lambda function as a subscriber.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS does not guarantee message order, so it cannot ensure ordered processing.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to hold messages. Set up an AWS Lambda function to process messages from the queue independently.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS standard queues do not preserve message order, which is a requirement.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to deliver notifications containing payloads to process. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a subscriber.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS does not guarantee message ordering, so ordering cannot be ensured even with an SQS subscriber.

questions.content:
A large media company hosts a web application on AWS. The company wants to start
caching confidential media files so that users around the world will have
reliable access to the files. The content is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The
company must deliver the content quickly, regardless of where the requests
originate geographically.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is used for data transfer and replication, not content caching or delivery.

answers.content: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves network performance but does not cache content or provide CDN features for S3 objects.

answers.content: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to connect the S3 buckets to CloudFront edge servers.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a managed content delivery network (CDN) service that caches content globally at edge locations to improve latency and reliability for users regardless of their geographic location. CloudFront is designed for securely delivering content stored in Amazon S3 buckets using Origin Access Control (OAC) to restrict direct bucket access and enable encrypted, authenticated access. Other options do not provide caching or global edge delivery of S3 content; CloudFront is the AWS best practice for caching and delivering confidential media files quickly and securely.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS is a message queuing service and cannot cache or deliver files.

questions.content:
A company needs to retain application log files for a critical application for
10 years. The application team regularly accesses logs from the past month for
troubleshooting, but logs older than 1 month are rarely accessed. The
application generates more than 10 TB of logs per month.
Which storage option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup is not the preferred or most cost-effective method to move S3 objects to Glacier Deep Archive compared to native S3 lifecycle policies.

answers.content: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 with lifecycle policies provides a managed and cost-effective solution for storing large volumes of logs. S3 Lifecycle policies can automatically transition logs older than 1 month to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which is a low-cost storage class for long-term retention. Using S3 avoids unnecessary costs associated with CloudWatch Logs storage for large amounts of data (more than 10 TB per month). Managed lifecycle policies are preferred over using AWS Backup for moving data between storage tiers, ensuring automation and cost efficiency.

answers.content: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: CloudWatch Logs is not ideal for storing very large volumes (over 10 TB per month) due to cost and does not natively support lifecycle transitions to Glacier Deep Archive.

answers.content: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: S3 lifecycle policies cannot be applied to CloudWatch Logs; lifecycle policies apply only to S3 storage, making this option invalid.

questions.content:
A company sells ringtones created from clips of popular songs. The files
containing the ringtones are stored in Amazon S3 Standard and are at least 128
KB in size. The company has millions of files, but downloads are infrequent for
ringtones older than 90 days. The company needs to save money on storage while
keeping the most accessed files readily available for its users.
Which action should the company take to meet these requirements MOST
cost-effectively?

answers.content: Configure S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage for the initial storage tier of the objects.
answers.explanation: Using S3 Standard-IA as the initial storage tier is not optimal because files are frequently accessed when newer than 90 days; starting with Standard storage is more cost-effective.

answers.content: Move the files to S3 Intelligent-Tiering and configure it to move objects to a less expensive storage tier after 90 days.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects to the most cost-effective tier but the question specifies files larger than 128 KB and a time-based transition, which Lifecycle policies address more explicitly and cost-efficiently.

answers.content: Configure S3 inventory to manage objects and move them to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-1A) after 90 days.
answers.explanation: S3 Inventory only provides reports and does not automate movement of objects; manual intervention would be needed, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy that moves the objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-1A) after 90 days.
answers.explanation: Implementing an S3 Lifecycle policy to move objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days aligns with cost optimization best practices by automatically transitioning infrequently accessed data to a lower-cost storage class. S3 Lifecycle policies are a managed AWS service feature for automated data tiering without manual effort. This option adheres to security best practices by not requiring additional manual processes or custom solutions. S3 Standard-IA is designed for objects accessed less frequently but requires rapid access when needed, fitting the use case of older ringtones.

questions.content:
A company is building a containerized application on premises and decides to
move the application to AWS. The application will have thousands of users soon
after it is deployed. The company is unsure how to manage the deployment of
containers at scale. The company needs to deploy the containerized application
in a highly available architecture that minimizes operational overhead.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the AWS Fargate launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
answers.explanation: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is the preferred managed service for storing container images. Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type allows running containers without managing the underlying EC2 instances, reducing operational overhead. Using target tracking for automatic scaling based on demand supports a highly available and scalable architecture. Managed AWS services like ECS with Fargate align with best practices to minimize operational overhead while supporting thousands of users.

answers.content: Store container images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Amazon EC2 launch type to run the containers. Use target tracking to scale automatically based on demand.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 launch type requires managing EC2 instances, increasing operational overhead compared to Fargate.

answers.content: Store container images in a repository that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Run the containers on EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Monitor the average CPU utilization in Amazon CloudWatch. Launch new EC2 instances as needed.
answers.explanation: Hosting container images on EC2 instances is less secure and less reliable than using Amazon ECR.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that contains the container image. Launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale out EC2 instances when the average CPU utilization threshold is breached.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 AMIs with containers and scaling based on CPU utilization involves more manual management and lacks container-specific scaling features.

questions.content:
A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The
application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages
in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent
traffic. This application should continually process messages without any
downtime.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
answers.explanation: Using only Spot Instances risks downtime due to interruptions, violating continuous processing requirement.

answers.content: Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
answers.explanation: Using only Reserved Instances might be cost-inefficient for unpredictable, spiky workloads.

answers.content: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
answers.explanation: Spot Instances are not ideal for critical workloads requiring continuous processing due to potential interruptions.

answers.content: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.
answers.explanation: Using Reserved Instances for baseline capacity ensures predictable costs for steady traffic. Using On-Demand Instances for additional capacity handles unpredictable traffic without risking instance interruption. Spot Instances are less reliable for unpredictable or continuous workloads due to possible interruptions. Balancing Reserved and On-Demand Instances aligns with cost-effectiveness and availability for variable workloads.

questions.content:
A security team wants to limit access to specific services or actions in all of
the team's AWS accounts. All accounts belong to a large organization in AWS
Organizations. The solution must be scalable and there must be a single point
where permissions can be maintained.

What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

answers.content: Create an ACL to provide access to the services or actions.
answers.explanation: ACLs manage network traffic, not IAM permissions or service access control across accounts.

answers.content: Create a security group to allow accounts and attach it to user groups.
answers.explanation: Security groups control network layer access within a VPC, not service or action permissions across AWS accounts.

answers.content: Create cross-account roles in each account to deny access to the services or actions.
answers.explanation: Cross-account roles require manual setup in each account and do not provide a single point of permission management; also, roles delegate access rather than deny it centrally.

answers.content: Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.
answers.explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) are designed to centrally manage permissions across all accounts in an AWS Organization. Applying SCPs at the root organizational unit provides a single scalable point of permission management that affects all member accounts. SCPs can restrict services or actions regardless of other permissions in individual accounts, aligning with the need to limit access organization-wide. This approach adheres to security best practices by enforcing least privilege centrally without relying on manual role creation or network configurations.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is optimizing a website for an upcoming musical event.
Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then will be
available on demand. The event is expected to attract a global online audience.

Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand
streaming?

answers.content: Amazon CloudFront
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network service designed to improve the performance of streaming videos both live and on-demand by caching content at edge locations close to viewers. CloudFront is purpose-built for video streaming workloads and optimizes delivery worldwide, which fits the scenario of a global online audience for both real-time and on-demand video. AWS Global Accelerator improves application availability and performance by directing traffic to the nearest regional endpoint, but it is not specifically designed for video streaming optimization or caching. Amazon Route 53 is primarily a DNS service and does not directly improve real-time or on-demand streaming performance. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes transfers to and from S3 buckets but does not enhance video streaming delivery performance globally.

answers.content: AWS Global Accelerator
answers.explanation: Improves application availability and network performance but is not specialized for video streaming optimization.

answers.content: Amazon Route 53
answers.explanation: DNS service that does not improve streaming performance or content delivery.

answers.content: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
answers.explanation: Optimizes upload and download speed to S3, not streaming performance for end users.

questions.content:
A company is running a publicly accessible serverless application that uses
Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The application's traffic recently spiked due
to fraudulent requests from botnets.

Which steps should a solutions architect take to block requests from
unauthorized users? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a usage plan with an API key that is shared with genuine users only.
answers.explanation: Correct; usage plans and API keys help control and limit access to authorized users.

answers.content: Integrate logic within the Lambda function to ignore the requests from fraudulent IP addresses.
answers.explanation: Incorrect; integrating logic in Lambda is custom and less efficient than managed WAF filtering, and processing malicious requests wastes resources.

answers.content: Implement an AWS WAF rule to target malicious requests and trigger actions to filter them out.
answers.explanation: Correct; AWS WAF is a managed service designed to filter malicious traffic at the edge before reaching API Gateway.

answers.content: Convert the existing public API to a private API. Update the DNS records to redirect users to the new API endpoint.
answers.explanation: Incorrect; converting the API to a private API restricts it to within a VPC, not suitable for a publicly accessible app with genuine users.

answers.content: E. Create an IAM role for each user attempting to access the API. A user will assume the role when making the API call.
answers.explanation: Incorrect; API Gateway does not support IAM role assumption per user for HTTP APIs and this is complex and does not prevent anonymous external requests.

questions.content:
A solutions architect is creating a new Amazon CloudFront distribution for an
application. Some of the information submitted by users is sensitive. The
application uses HTTPS but needs another layer of security. The sensitive
information should.be protected throughout the entire application stack, and
access to the information should be restricted to certain applications.

Which action should the solutions architect take?

answers.content: Configure a CloudFront signed URL.
answers.explanation: CloudFront signed URLs restrict access to content but do not provide extra encryption for sensitive fields.

answers.content: Configure a CloudFront signed cookie.
answers.explanation: CloudFront signed cookies also manage access control but do not encrypt specific sensitive data fields.

answers.content: Configure a CloudFront field-level encryption profile.
answers.explanation: Field-level encryption in CloudFront adds an additional layer of security by encrypting sensitive specific data fields throughout the application stack, ensuring that sensitive information is protected end-to-end. CloudFront signed URLs or signed cookies control access but do not provide per-field encryption of sensitive data within the content. Using HTTPS secures data in transit, but field-level encryption protects sensitive data even within internal application layers. The question specifies that sensitive information should be protected throughout the entire stack and access restricted to certain applications, which field-level encryption specifically addresses.

answers.content: Configure CloudFront and set the Origin Protocol Policy setting to HTTPS Only for the Viewer Protocol Policy.
answers.explanation: Origin Protocol Policy to HTTPS Only ensures secure transport but does not provide additional data encryption or access control for sensitive fields.

questions.content:
Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML
pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around
the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect
has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution.

Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?

answers.content: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
answers.explanation: Presigned URLs are not suitable for millions of global views due to complexity and lack of caching benefits.

answers.content: Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
answers.explanation: Cross-Region replication duplicates data but does not provide efficient global delivery or reduce latency like a CDN.

answers.content: Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
answers.explanation: Amazon Route 53 geoproximity routing controls traffic direction but does not cache content or improve static website delivery efficiency.

answers.content: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a global content delivery network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations, providing low latency access to S3-backed static websites for millions of global viewers. Using CloudFront with the S3 bucket as the origin is efficient and effective for serving static content with high availability and scalability. CloudFront supports secure access to buckets encrypted with SSE-KMS when using origin access control (OAC), which aligns with security best practices. This approach is preferred over methods like presigned URLs or cross-region replication, which are not optimal for high traffic static website delivery.

questions.content:
A company has two applications: a sender application that sends messages with
payloads to be processed and a processing application intended to receive the
messages with payloads. The company wants to implement an AWS service to handle
messages between the two applications. The sender application can send about
1,000 messages each hour. The messages may take up to 2 days to be processed: If
the messages fail to process, they must be retained so that they do not impact
the processing of any remaining messages.

Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

answers.content: Set up an Amazon EC2 instance running a Redis database. Configure both applications to use the instance. Store, process, and delete the messages, respectively.
answers.explanation: Managing a Redis database on EC2 is operationally intensive and not a managed messaging service, thus less operationally efficient.

answers.content: Use an Amazon Kinesis data stream to receive the messages from the sender application. Integrate the processing application with the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).
answers.explanation: Kinesis is more complex and intended for streaming large volumes of data with lower latency, overkill for 1,000 messages per hour and less operationally efficient for delayed processing.

answers.content: Integrate the sender and processor applications with an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure a dead-letter queue to collect the messages that failed to process.
answers.explanation: Amazon SQS is designed to decouple distributed applications and supports message retention up to 14 days. SQS ensures messages are retained if processing fails by using dead-letter queues, which meet the requirement of retaining failed messages without impacting other messages. SQS is fully managed, providing operational efficiency and offloading infrastructure management from the company. Other options either do not provide message retention or require more manual management and operational effort compared to SQS.

answers.content: Subscribe the processing application to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive notifications to process. Integrate the sender application to write to the SNS topic.
answers.explanation: SNS does not provide message retention or dead-letter queues; messages are delivered immediately and not stored if processing fails.

questions.content:
A solutions architect must design a solution that uses Amazon CloudFront with an
Amazon S3 origin to store a static website. The company's security policy
requires that all website traffic be inspected by AWS WAF.

How should the solutions architect comply with these requirements?

answers.content: Configure an S3 bucket policy to accept requests coming from the AWS WAF Amazon Resource Name (ARN) only.
answers.explanation: S3 bucket policies cannot restrict access by AWS WAF ARN as WAF is attached to CloudFront, not S3.

answers.content: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward all incoming requests to AWS WAF before requesting content from the S3 origin.
answers.explanation: CloudFront forwards requests to the origin directly; it does not forward requests to WAF separately, as WAF is integrated with CloudFront.

answers.content: Configure a security group that allows Amazon CloudFront IP addresses to access Amazon S3 only. Associate AWS WAF to CloudFront.
answers.explanation: Security groups do not control S3 bucket access because S3 is a managed service without VPC security groups; also, WAF must be associated directly with CloudFront.

answers.content: Configure Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to use an origin access identity (OAI) to restrict access to the S3 bucket. Enable AWS WAF on the distribution.
answers.explanation: Security best practices recommend restricting S3 bucket access to only CloudFront using origin access control (OAC), which is an updated and preferred method over OAI. Enabling AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution ensures that all incoming website traffic is inspected as required by the company policy. Configuring the S3 bucket to be accessible only via CloudFront prevents direct access, ensuring traffic goes through WAF-enabled CloudFront. AWS managed services like CloudFront and WAF provide integrated, secure solutions for serving static websites with inspection.

questions.content:
A company is concerned about the security of its public web application due to
recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A
solutions architect must reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the
application.

What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

answers.content: Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector is for vulnerability assessments, not for preventing DDoS attacks on ALB.

answers.content: Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.
answers.explanation: Amazon Macie is designed for data security and privacy, not for preventing DDoS attacks.

answers.content: Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
answers.explanation: AWS Shield Advanced provides protection against DDoS attacks and can be enabled to protect Application Load Balancers using threat intelligence and traffic pattern analysis. It has modes that activate protection automatically under DDoS conditions or always-on mode, actively rate-limiting traffic from known malicious sources, minimizing impact on legitimate traffic. This leverages built-in AWS managed DDoS mitigation services which is preferred over manual or unrelated services.

answers.content: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.
answers.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is for threat detection and monitoring, not active DDoS protection.

questions.content:
A company's web application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an
Application Load Balancer. The company recently changed its policy, which now
requires the application to be accessed from one specific country only.

Which configuration will meet this requirement?

answers.content: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Security groups cannot filter traffic by geographic location; they filter by IP, port, and protocol only.

answers.content: Configure the security group on the Application Load Balancer.
answers.explanation: Security groups on ALB do not support geo-based access controls.

answers.content: Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF can be configured on the Application Load Balancer to filter requests based on geographic location, which is the most effective way to restrict access by country. Security groups and network ACLs do not natively support geographic restrictions. AWS WAF is a managed service designed for web application filtering and security, aligning with AWS best practices to use managed services. Implementing location-based filtering at the ALB level ensures all incoming requests are inspected before reaching the instances.

answers.content: Configure the network ACL for the subnet that contains the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Network ACLs also do not have built-in geographic filtering capabilities and are less flexible for this requirement.

questions.content:
A company provides an API to its users that automates inquiries for tax
computations based on item prices. The company experiences a larger number of
inquiries during the holiday season only that cause slower response times. A
solutions architect needs to design a solution that is scalable and elastic.

What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

answers.content: Provide an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance performs the required computations when the API request is made.
answers.explanation: An EC2 instance alone does not automatically scale and would likely become a bottleneck during high traffic.

answers.content: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that accepts the item names. API Gateway passes item names to AWS Lambda for tax computations.
answers.explanation: Amazon API Gateway combined with AWS Lambda provides a fully managed, serverless, and elastic solution that automatically scales with demand. AWS Lambda eliminates the need for managing servers and ensures automatic scaling during peak loads, such as the holiday season. API Gateway efficiently handles REST API requests and integrates seamlessly with Lambda for lightweight computation tasks. This approach aligns with AWS best practices favoring managed services over EC2 instances for scalability and elasticity.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer that has two Amazon EC2 instances behind it. The EC2 instances will compute the tax on the received item names.
answers.explanation: Using only two EC2 instances behind a load balancer offers limited scalability and does not automatically handle large traffic spikes.

answers.content: Design a REST API using Amazon API Gateway that connects with an API hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance. API Gateway accepts and passes the item names to the EC2 instance for tax computations.
answers.explanation: Using an EC2 instance behind API Gateway still requires managing and scaling EC2 instances manually, reducing elasticity.

questions.content:
A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the
application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in
Amazon S3. This content is the same for all users.

The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide
accessing these media files. The company wants to provide the files to the users
while reducing the load on the origin.

Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves availability and performance for applications but does not cache content or reduce origin load like CloudFront.

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is designed to deliver content with low latency and high transfer speeds globally. CloudFront caches content at edge locations, reducing load on the origin S3 bucket. The content is static and the same for all users, making CloudFront caching ideal and cost-effective. AWS best practices recommend CloudFront for delivering S3 content to global users. Other options do not provide a global caching and content delivery solution as cost-effectively.

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis is for in-memory caching of database queries or session data, not optimized for static content delivery or global caching.

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Memcached has similar limitations as Redis and is not designed for global content delivery or reducing S3 origin load.

questions.content:
A company has a multi-tier application that runs six front-end web servers in an
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone behind an
Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect needs to modify the
infrastructure to be highly available without modifying the application.

Which architecture should the solutions architect choose that provides high
availability?

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses three instances across each of two Regions.
answers.explanation: Deploying across multiple Regions is complex and may require modifying the application for cross-Region replication and routing.

answers.content: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use three instances across each of two Availability Zones.
answers.explanation: Using multiple Availability Zones within the same Region provides high availability without needing to modify the application. Auto Scaling across multiple Availability Zones ensures fault tolerance in case an AZ fails. An Application Load Balancer supports distributing traffic across multiple AZs enabling this architecture. Managing instances within a single Region minimizes complexity compared to multi-Region setups, which would require application changes.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling template that can be used to quickly create more instances in another Region.
answers.explanation: Creating a template alone does not provide high availability without active deployment and load balancing across AZs or Regions.

answers.content: Change the ALB in front of the Amazon EC2 instances in a round-robin configuration to balance traffic to the web tier.
answers.explanation: Changing ALB to round-robin does not address single Availability Zone failure; ALB already distributes traffic across healthy instances.

questions.content:
An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application
needs to access an Amazon DynamoDB table.

What is the MOST secure way to access the table while ensuring that the traffic
does not leave the AWS network?

answers.content: Use a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: Using a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB ensures that traffic between the EC2 instances and the DynamoDB table stays within the AWS network and does not traverse the public internet. This method leverages managed AWS infrastructure designed for secure, private connectivity to AWS services. Using NAT gateway or NAT instance routes traffic through the internet and is not as secure because it exposes traffic to the public internet. Internet gateway by definition routes traffic out to the internet, which violates the requirement that traffic does not leave the AWS network.

answers.content: Use a NAT gateway in a public subnet.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway routes traffic through the internet, so traffic leaves the AWS network, which is not secure.

answers.content: Use a NAT instance in a private subnet.
